h1: The 7 Best Cordless Stick Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Stick Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven cordless stick vacuums from Shark and value brands, compared on listed run time, wattage and price tier.
summary: The Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus is the best cordless stick vacuum for most buyers, combining a 50 minute run time with a major brand at a mid price. JELLYPIG, Uosogi and SMOTURE list 70 minutes and 650W for similar money. The KARDV is the budget pick, and the Shark Pet suits smaller homes.
intro: A run time printed in bold on the box is almost never what you get with the vacuum doing real work. The headline figure is normally the gentlest power mode, so a model advertised at 70 minutes may last a fraction of that when you switch to the setting that lifts carpet debris. Treat every listed minute count as a best case.

We reviewed seven cordless stick vacuums on paper, comparing listed run time, wattage, brand and price bucket. Two Shark Pet listings share a name at different prices, so we counted that model once and flagged the overlap. Where a listing gave no wattage or capacity, we left the gap in place instead of filling it with guesses.

products.name: Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: The best-known brand with a 50 minute run time in the mid bucket.
products.description:
The Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus is a cordless stick vacuum with a listed 50 minute run time, sold in the $100 to $200 bucket. It comes from a manufacturer with an established service network and parts supply.

First place goes to it because brand support counts for more than extra minutes on a machine that will see daily use. The value brands below list noticeably longer run times and a stated 650W, so the Shark does not win on the spec sheet. It wins on the likelihood that you can still find a replacement filter or battery in three years.

Buy it if you want a recognizable name and dependable warranty access. Skip it if you want the longest listed run time, or if you need a wattage figure, because the listing does not give one.
cons: Less run time than value brands
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer a major brand.
products.skipIf: You want the longest listed run time.

products.name: JELLYPIG Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: 70 minutes and 650W listed, from a value brand.
products.description:
JELLYPIG lists a 70 minute run time and 650W of power in a cordless body, also in the $100 to $200 bucket. On numbers alone it beats everything else near its price.

It trails the Shark because a value brand brings less certainty about long-term parts and service, and a 70 minute figure almost certainly reflects the lowest power mode. Against its two twins below, it holds the top slot only by being listed first in our research. The data gives no true tiebreaker among the three.

Buy it for a large home where long sessions matter and brand reputation is secondary. Skip it if you want established support. Treat the 650W rating as a rough indicator of motor strength, not a promise of suction, and check the warranty terms in the listing before ordering.
cons: Max run time likely uses low mode

products.name: Uosogi Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: Same listed 70 minutes and 650W as JELLYPIG.
products.description:
The Uosogi lists 70 minutes of run time and 650W, cordless, in the $100 to $200 bucket. Those are exactly the same figures as the JELLYPIG.

It sits third because nothing in the facts separates it from the model above. Both are value-brand sticks with matching specs, so the practical advice is to buy whichever is cheaper on the day you shop. The difference between them is more likely to come from seller reliability and return policy than from anything printed in the spec sheet.

Buy it if you are comparing value brands on price alone. Skip it if you want a brand with established service, since the Shark above offers that at a similar bucket. If the Uosogi is listed noticeably above the JELLYPIG when you check, treat that as a reason to switch, not a mark of quality.

products.name: SMOTURE Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: Another 70 minute, 650W cordless in the same bucket.
products.description:
SMOTURE is the third near twin in this group, listing 70 minutes and 650W, cordless, in the $100 to $200 bucket.

Fourth position reflects the fact that it brings nothing the JELLYPIG and Uosogi lack. If anything, the crowded field of identical specs is the main finding: three brands with the same numbers means you should expect to choose on price, shipping and return terms. The ranking here is a coin flip decided by research order, not a verdict on quality.

Buy it if it happens to be the cheapest of the three at checkout. Skip it if you would rather have a more differentiated machine. A model like the KARDV costs less and lists less, while the Shark gives you a major brand. Neither of those options is a worse choice than this one, only a different trade.

products.name: KARDV Cordless Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: The lowest price tier here with 60 minutes and 500W listed.
products.description:
KARDV is the budget entry, with a listed 60 minute run time and 500W, cordless, in the $50 to $100 bucket, the cheapest of the group.

It sits fifth because it lists fewer watts than the 650W machines, though it still reaches 60 minutes of claimed run time and costs a full price tier less. For an apartment or a car, the saving matters more than 150W of rated power. The weakness is the same as every value brand here: little to prove it will last.

Buy it for quick cleanups, hard floors and small spaces where you want the lowest outlay. Skip it if you need the strongest suction for thick carpet. Compare it carefully with the three 650W models, which cost more but list considerably higher wattage, and consider whether the extra cost buys anything you would actually notice.

products.name: Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: A Shark with a 40 minute listed run time.
products.description:
The Shark Pet Cordless Stick lists a 40 minute run time and sits in the $100 to $200 bucket. The pet-focused name suggests brushes aimed at hair, though our facts do not describe the head.

Sixth place comes from the run time. Forty minutes is the shortest in the group, and the PowerPro offers ten more at the same bucket. A second listing with the same name sits in the $200 to $500 bucket, so make sure you open the right page before you pay. Mixing them up is the easy mistake with this model.

Buy it if you want a Shark for a smaller home and the pet branding appeals. Skip it if you clean large floors in one go, since 40 minutes is a modest budget. Confirm the exact model number before checkout, because two listings appear under one name.

products.name: Shark Cordless Vacuum Cleaner - Blue - IZ363HT
products.verdict: A 50 minute Shark in the highest price bucket here.
products.description:
The Shark IZ363HT is a cordless stick with a listed 50 minute run time, in the $200 to $500 bucket, the highest price tier here. The model number is specific, which helps when comparing listings.

It lands last because the cheaper PowerPro offers the same 50 minutes for a full price tier less. Nothing in the facts explains what the extra money buys, such as a larger bin or different attachments. Without that, the premium is hard to justify for most buyers.

Buy it if you are set on this exact model, perhaps because you have used it or found a favorable deal. Skip it if value matters at all. Check what accessories and warranty the page lists, since those are the only possible reasons to pay more than for the PowerPro.
cons: Same run time as cheaper Shark
products.idealFor: Fans of this specific Shark model.

whatMatters.detail: Run time is how long one charge lasts, almost always at the lowest power setting. It matters because stronger modes drain the battery faster and the real figure on carpet is shorter. Find the minutes in the title or bullets and treat them as a best case. Value brands here list up to 70 minutes.

Wattage is a rough sign of motor power, though it does not translate directly into suction at the floor. It is useful only when comparing similar designs. Find the number in the listing. JELLYPIG, Uosogi and SMOTURE list 650W, KARDV lists 500W, and the Shark listings give no wattage.

Brand support covers parts, filters, batteries and warranty service. A known brand usually makes these easier to find years later, while value brands may disappear. Check the seller's warranty details on the listing. This is the main reason the Shark PowerPro leads, despite shorter listed minutes than the value brands.

Price tier is the bucket the vacuum sells in. Higher tiers do not always mean longer run time or more power, as the $200 to $500 IZ363HT lists the same 50 minutes as the cheaper PowerPro. Compare minutes and watts per bucket before deciding, and pay extra only for a stated reason.

Duplicate listings happen when a model appears under the same name at different prices. The Shark Pet is the example here, with two pages in different buckets. Open the exact listing and compare model numbers, because the cheaper one may be an older or different configuration.

faq.q: Does the listed run time apply to every mode?
faq.a: No. The listed minutes are usually the longest figure, reached at low power. The 70 minutes quoted for the JELLYPIG would likely shrink on its strongest setting, so plan on shorter sessions on thick carpet.

faq.q: Are the three 650W models the same?
faq.a: Their listed numbers match at 70 minutes and 650W, and the facts give no tiebreaker among JELLYPIG, Uosogi and SMOTURE. Choose by price, shipping speed and return policy on the day you buy.

faq.q: Is a Shark worth it over a value brand?
faq.a: If brand support matters, yes. The Shark PowerPro offers an established name with 50 minutes. If run time matters most, the value brands list up to 70, and the KARDV costs less still.

faq.q: How do I check which Shark Pet I am buying?
faq.a: Two listings share the name at different price tiers, in the $100 to $200 and $200 to $500 buckets. Compare model details and check the number before ordering so you know which Shark Pet you are actually buying.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cordless vacuum?
faq.a: Empty the bin after each use and clean the filter and brush. Charge the battery regularly but avoid leaving it fully drained or hot for long periods. Follow the manual for whichever model you choose, from the KARDV to the Shark.

faq.q: Can I use these on every floor type?
faq.a: The facts we reviewed do not state supported floor types for these vacuums. Check each listing for hard floor and carpet details before ordering, especially for the value brands where specifications are sparse.

finalTake: For most buyers the Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus is the cordless stick vacuum to buy, because its 50 minute run time comes with a brand you can rely on for parts. If you care more about raw numbers, pick whichever of the three 650W value models costs least. Choose the KARDV for the smallest budget, and treat every listed run time as a best case.
